# Studienstiftung
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, initially founded in 1925 and re-established in 1948, is a prestigious German scholarship foundation offering both financial and academic support to exceptionally talented undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students. Admission is highly selective and occurs via multiple channels including school and professor nominations, examination boards, national competition winners, self-application through an assessment test, alumni nominations, and support for musicians and artists. The scholarship supports full-time university studies primarily in Germany, other EU countries, or Switzerland, and is not restricted by citizenship or age.
Financially, scholarship holders receive monthly allowances and health insurance subsidies, with need-based grants available. Doctoral candidates receive a higher stipend plus research allowances. Academically, the foundation offers workshops, summer schools, mentoring, and supports scholar-organized events. Extensions beyond initial funding depend on academic performance and social engagement. The foundation also collaborates on special programs like the KAUST-Studienstiftung partnership. In 2023, about 2,179 scholarships and 301 doctoral scholarships were awarded, with slightly more than half of the scholars being women. Notable alumni include Nobel laureates and leading figures in sciences, social sciences, business, politics, arts, and journalism.
